GitHub Issue #196: Chat preamble claims guidance skills are installed when seeding installed nothing

Issue URL: https://github.com/sociotechnica-org/skillmaker-studio/issues/196

## Summary

The chat preamble tells every agent "Your guidance skills are installed in your
agent home -- read the relevant william-* skill before acting." When seeding
installed nothing, that sentence is false, and the agent does what a competent
agent should: it goes looking for the skills it was promised. `prepareAgentHome`
already returns exactly the fact needed to tell the truth — `installedHelpers` —
and the call site throws it away.

## Motivation / Problem

An instruction that names an artifact which isn't there is worse than no
instruction: it converts a missing dependency into a filesystem search. In the
live session that produced this ticket, the agent's first move was
`ls ~/.skillmaker/agent-home/claude-code/skills/`, and when that came back
empty it escalated to `find / -maxdepth 8 -type d -iname "william-*"` and a
sweep of the operator's other repos. Each of those is a path outside the
project, so each one raised a permission card.

This is a *distinct* defect from the seeding bug (#190). Fixing #190 makes the
helpers present in shipped builds — but a source checkout with no packaged
skills directory, or a future helper slug that fails to resolve, will still be
announced as installed. The preamble should assert only what is true at the
moment it is written.

## Observed behavior

Fresh project on v0.6.2, chat session started on a new bundle. The agent home
contains no `skills/` directory. The preamble nonetheless states the skills are
installed, and the session opens with a multi-command hunt across the machine
for `william-*` before any bundle work begins.

## Current shape

The claim, `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts:324`:

```ts
    `- Your guidance skills are installed in your agent home -- read the relevant william-* skill before acting.`,
```

It is unconditional — a constant line in the preamble array, with no input from
whether seeding succeeded.

Meanwhile `prepareAgentHome` computes and returns precisely that
(`ChatSessions.ts:160`, `:179-181`):

```ts
): { readonly home: string; readonly installedHelpers: ReadonlyArray<string> } => {
```
```ts
    installed.push(slug);
  }
  return { home, installedHelpers: installed };
```

and both call sites discard it — `ChatSessions.ts:598` and `:793`:

```ts
    const { home } = prepareAgentHome(provider, this.root, this.config.skillsDir);
```

The trap worth naming: the information needed to be honest is already computed,
already returned, and already at the call site. This is not a missing capability;
it is a discarded return value.

## Proposed contract

The helper line is conditional on what actually installed:

| `installedHelpers` | Preamble line |
|---|---|
| non-empty | `- Your guidance skills (<slugs>) are installed in your agent home -- read the relevant one before acting.` |
| empty | line omitted entirely |

**Decisions:**

- When helpers installed, the line **names the slugs actually present**, so the
  agent reads what exists rather than guessing at a family name.
- When none installed, the line is **omitted**, not replaced with an apology.
  An agent told nothing about guidance skills proceeds on the bundle; an agent
  told they are "missing" may go hunting anyway.
- Partial installs name only the slugs that landed.
- `installedHelpers` is threaded to the preamble builder. `PreambleContext`
  gains a field; no other preamble line changes.
- The re-orientation preamble (`buildChatReorientation`, `ChatSessions.ts:349`)
  does not mention helpers today and does not gain a mention.
- No UI, no journal event, no warning surface. The scope is the preamble string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With helpers installed, the preamble states they are installed and names
      the installed slugs.
- [ ] With no helpers installed, the preamble contains no sentence asserting
      guidance skills are available anywhere.
- [ ] Partial install: only the slugs that actually landed are named.
- [ ] Negative: the preamble never names a slug absent from the agent home.
- [ ] Regression: every other preamble line — bundle layout, pipeline, CLI
      guidance, direct-in-project warning, and the derived-stage "current step"
      sentence — is byte-identical to today.
- [ ] Regression: `packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts` passes, extended
      rather than rewritten.
- [ ] Regression: `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` is unchanged — the viewer splits replayed
      first prompts on it (`chatModel.ts`).
- [ ] Tests cover: helpers-present, helpers-absent, and partial-install.

## Implementation notes

Both call sites already destructure the result; the change is to keep the second
field and pass it through. Prefer threading it into `PreambleContext` over
recomputing installation state inside the preamble builder — the builder is
deliberately synchronous and filesystem-light.

Scope fences:

- **Do not fix the seeding here.** That is #190. This issue is about the
  preamble telling the truth about whatever seeding did.
- **Do not add a user-facing warning.** A missing helper is not a condition the
  director needs a banner for.
- **Do not change `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` or the separator** — the viewer parses on
  both.

Relevant current files, as orientation only:

- `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts` — the claim (:324), the preamble
  builder (:320-329), `prepareAgentHome` (:156-182), call sites (:598, :793)
- `packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts` — existing coverage

---

**Related:** #190 (packaged-skills fallback for the agent home). #190 makes the
helpers present; this makes the preamble honest when they aren't.


Implement exactly this issue. Verify every claim in the issue against the current code before acting on it; the issue is a report, not a spec — the code is the truth. Stay minimal: fix the reported defect with tests, nothing adjacent.

# ReviewJudge

You are the single review-and-verdict gate before the PR. Review the
implementation diff against the scope plan (under `docs/proposals/`, named
by the scope stage) and the house rules, read the gates output from the
previous stage, and deliver ONE verdict. Do not edit any files.

Check:

- The diff stays within the plan's scope and package boundaries: domain
  logic and schemas in `packages/core`, deterministic CLI/server behavior
  in `packages/cli`, browser UI in `packages/viewer`.
- Comments are plain English prose explaining WHY, citing issues, dated
  proposals, and rulings (`packages/core/src/Todo.ts` is the standard).
- Behavior changes have tests (black-box CLI tests for CLI behavior,
  `test/e2e` for server-surface changes).
- No files under `docs/library` were freehand-edited outside an approved
  library migration.
- The deterministic gates output shows the repo gates passed on the final
  diff.

Grading bar — this line is load-bearing: a mergeable change with noted
imperfections is a PASSING grade — perfectionism is the expensive failure
mode; note imperfections in the PR body instead of bouncing. Only route
Fix for real defects: broken or untested behavior, scope/plan mismatch,
boundary violations, failing gates. Style nits, minor gaps, and "could be
better" observations go in a short "Imperfections to note in the PR body"
list in your response, which the Prepare PR stage will include.

Verdicts (exactly one):

- **ready** — the change is mergeable. List any imperfections for the PR
  body, then route to Prepare PR.
- **fix** — a real defect blocks merge. Allowed AT MOST ONCE per run (the
  graph enforces this: this node runs at most twice, so on your second
  run Fix is off the table — choose ready or surface). Give concrete,
  actionable fix items so the implement stage can act without guessing.
- **surface** — you and the implementation cannot converge (e.g. the fix
  round did not resolve the defect, or the plan itself is wrong). Stop
  the run with a clear summary of the disagreement for a human.

End with exactly one routing JSON object:

```json
{"preferred_next_label":"Ready","context_updates":{"verdict":"ready"}}
```

or:

```json
{"preferred_next_label":"Fix","context_updates":{"verdict":"fix"}}
```

or:

```json
{"preferred_next_label":"Surface","outcome":"failed","failure_reason":"<one-line summary of the disagreement>","context_updates":{"verdict":"surface"}}
```

# Scope

Write a durable technical implementation plan for the requested
Skillmaker Studio feature to
`docs/proposals/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<stable-feature-slug>.md` (refine an
existing relevant plan instead of duplicating it). Do not edit
implementation files in this stage.

## The repository

Skillmaker Studio is a bun + Effect TypeScript monorepo (bun workspaces):

- `packages/core` — the domain engine: skills, evals, journal, todos,
  triage. Effect-first; schemas live here and everything else consumes
  them.
- `packages/cli` — the `skillmaker` CLI and the local server the Studio
  UI rides on. Command data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, stable
  exit codes.
- `packages/viewer` — the Studio browser UI (Astro + React).
- `packages/desktop`, `packages/docs-site`, `packages/marketing-site`,
  `packages/skill` — touch these only when the goal names them.
- `test/e2e` — black-box end-to-end tests over the CLI and server
  surfaces.
- `docs/proposals/` — dated proposal/plan documents. Do not
  freehand-edit `docs/library` (the live product context library)
  unless the plan explicitly owns a library migration.

Repository gates (mirrors `.github/workflows/ci.yml`): typecheck core
and cli, `bun test packages`, `bun test test/e2e`, and
`bun run build:viewer` when the viewer changes. A script node runs these
after implementation; plan work that passes them.

House comment style — plan for it now so implementation inherits it:
comments are plain English prose that explains WHY the code is shaped
this way, not what it does, and cites sources — issue numbers, dated
proposals, rulings — the way `packages/core/src/Todo.ts` does.

## Plan expectations

- Keep work scoped to the packages and surfaces named by the goal, with
  domain logic in core, deterministic CLI/server behavior in cli,
  browser UI state in viewer.
- Include tests for changed behavior, and risks, acceptance criteria,
  and deferred follow-ups.

End your response with `Plan ready for implementation: <plan-path>` and
a brief summary; the implement stage reads the plan file from disk.

# Implement

Implement the plan under `docs/proposals/` named by the scope stage.
Package-local README/guidance files own workflow and testing for the
packages you touch.

Rules:

- Stay scoped to the plan and its package boundaries: domain logic and
  schemas in `packages/core`, deterministic CLI/server behavior in
  `packages/cli` (data on stdout, diagnostics on stderr, stable exit
  codes, black-box tests for behavior), browser UI state in
  `packages/viewer`. If the plan cannot be implemented coherently
  without expanding scope, implement the smallest coherent slice and
  leave a clear blocking note in your final response.
- Do not freehand-edit `docs/library` (the live product context
  library) unless the plan explicitly owns a library migration.
- Comments in the house style: plain English prose explaining WHY,
  citing issues, dated proposals, and rulings, the way
  `packages/core/src/Todo.ts` does.
- If you are here after a gate failure or a ReviewJudge fix verdict,
  read that stage's output from context and fix exactly what it names.
  Retries are capped in the graph, so make the fix count.

Gates. Before finishing, run and pass ALL of:

```bash
bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/core
bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/cli
bun test packages
bun test test/e2e --timeout 30000
```

AND, whenever the diff touches `packages/viewer`:

```bash
bun run build:viewer
```

A script node reruns the same gates right after this stage; a failure
routes straight back here. Summarize the implemented changes at the end.

# Prepare PR

Prepare the final pull request context.

Fabro's configured `[run.pull_request]` finalization creates the pull
request after this node. Write the PR title and body to these files:

- `/tmp/fabro-pr-title.txt`
- `/tmp/fabro-pr-body.md`

The body must be honest reviewer context, not a sales pitch. Include:

- Suggested PR title.
- What changed and why, tied to the plan in `docs/proposals/`.
- Validation: which gates ran (typecheck core/cli, `bun test packages`,
  `bun test test/e2e`, `bun run build:viewer` if the viewer changed) and
  their actual results.
- The ReviewJudge's "imperfections to note in the PR body" list, carried
  over verbatim from that stage's output. Noted imperfections are the
  deal — the judge passes mergeable-with-notes changes on the promise
  that the notes reach the reviewer.
- Any remaining risks, known gaps, skipped checks, or manual follow-up —
  stated plainly. If something was not verified, say so; do not imply
  coverage that does not exist.

Keep the summary concise and specific to Skillmaker Studio. Do not
describe this as a handoff to a human; write it as PR-ready reviewer
context.

The title file must contain exactly one line. The body file must contain
Markdown suitable for a draft pull request body.

+# Honest Chat Helper Preamble
+
+*Implementation plan — 2026-08-04. GitHub issue #196. Run
+`01KZ77BKMTF836C1KHDHAES1M2`.*
+
+## Status
+
+Ready for implementation. This is a narrowly scoped CLI/server prompt
+correction with focused unit and chat-session integration coverage. It does
+not change helper seeding, the viewer, chat wire delimiters, or any
+user-facing surface.
+
+## Outcome
+
+The first-prompt chat preamble will describe only the guidance helpers that
+`prepareAgentHome` installed for that live session:
+
+| Session-start `installedHelpers` | Preamble behavior |
+|---|---|
+| Two or more slugs | Include one guidance bullet naming every returned slug, in returned order and separated by `, `. |
+| One slug | Include the same bullet naming only that slug. |
+| Empty | Omit the guidance bullet completely. |
+
+The rendered non-empty form is:
+
+```text
+- Your guidance skills (<comma-separated slugs>) are installed in your agent home -- read the relevant one before acting.
+```
+
+There is no missing-helper apology or warning. A preamble with an empty list
+simply proceeds from the pipeline bullet to the existing CLI bullet.
+
+## Verified current state
+
+The issue's defect is present in the current code:
+
+- `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts` defines
+  `HELPER_SKILL_SLUGS` as `william-research-a-skill` and
+  `william-draft-skill-md`.
+- `prepareAgentHome` independently resolves and copies each helper, pushes a
+  slug only after its copy completes, and returns
+  `{ home, installedHelpers }`.
+- `buildChatPreamble` currently emits the unconditional
+  `william-*` guidance bullet even when the returned list is empty or
+  partial.
+- Both current `prepareAgentHome` callers destructure only `home`. The
+  capability-probe caller never constructs a preamble; the real
+  `startSession` caller is the result that must be retained.
+- A fresh full preamble can be built later through either
+  `sendOrientationOpening` or the first-message branch in `sendMessage`.
+  Consequently, a local variable at `startSession` is insufficient; the
+  installation result must live with the live session.
+- A genuine resume uses `buildChatReorientation`, which has no helper claim
+  and must remain unchanged. A resume fallback has `resumed: false` and
+  correctly takes a fresh-preamble path.
+- `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` is currently
+  `You're inside Skillmaker Studio.`, and `PREAMBLE_SEPARATOR` is
+  `\n\n---\n\n`. The viewer's replay splitting in
+  `packages/viewer/src/app/next/chatModel.ts` depends on those exact values.
+- `packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts` currently passes 20 tests but
+  assumes the William guidance line is unconditional.
+- `test/e2e/chat-sessions.e2e.test.ts` already creates only
+  `william-draft-skill-md`. It is therefore an existing partial-install
+  fixture that can verify the session-start result reaches both full-preamble
+  paths without adding a new harness.
+
+There is no existing proposal dedicated to issue #196, so this plan does not
+duplicate another dated plan.
+
+One issue-report phrase needs a code-truth refinement: the capability probe
+may continue discarding `installedHelpers` because it has no preamble
+consumer. Only the real session-start result must cross the delayed prompt
+boundary. Also, “true when written” means the installation result captured
+at session start; this change deliberately does not rescan the agent home
+before every prompt.
+
+## Design and data flow
+
+Keep `installedHelpers` as a required, readonly list at every boundary where
+the full preamble can be built:
+
+```text
+prepareAgentHome during startSession
+  -> LiveChat.installedHelpers
+     -> readPreambleContext(..., installedHelpers)
+        -> buildChatPreamble
+           -> conditional guidance bullet
+```
+
+`LiveChat` is the bridge because the first prompt may be sent after
+`startSession` returns. Store exactly the array returned by that session's
+preparation. Do not infer from `HELPER_SKILL_SLUGS`, inspect the filesystem
+again, or use the earlier capability-probe result.
+
+Add `installedHelpers: ReadonlyArray<string>` to `PreambleContext`. Make
+`readPreambleContext` accept the session's installed-helper list and return it
+with the existing one-liner, declared stage, and artifact-derived stage. Keep
+the parameter required rather than defaulting it: a required input makes a
+future full-preamble call site account for installation state instead of
+silently recreating the unconditional-claim defect.
+
+`buildChatPreamble` will spread either one guidance-line element or no
+elements into its existing line array. This avoids an empty array element and
+therefore avoids introducing an extra blank line when no helpers installed.
+It will use `context.installedHelpers.join(", ")` without sorting or expanding
+the known helper family, so partial installation can never name a helper that
+the preparation result omitted.
+
+`buildChatReorientation` continues to accept `PreambleContext` for its
+existing stage facts but does not read or render `installedHelpers`.
+
+## Implementation plan
+
+### 1. Retain the session-start installation result
+
+In `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts`:
+
+1. Add an `installedHelpers: ReadonlyArray<string>` field to `LiveChat`.
+   Initialize it safely for the existing start sequence, then assign the
+   exact list returned when the real `startSession` call destructures
+   `{ home, installedHelpers }`.
+2. Keep the capability-probe destructuring as `{ home }`. Retaining an unused
+   list there would not improve preamble correctness.
+3. Do not move preparation into the prompt builders. It includes auth seeding
+   and helper copying and must remain a session-start operation.
+4. If a field comment is useful, explain why the session-start snapshot must
+   survive until the delayed first prompt and cite issue #196. Do not add a
+   comment that merely narrates the assignment.
+
+### 2. Thread the fact through both full-preamble paths
+
+In the same file:
+
+1. Add the required `installedHelpers` field to `PreambleContext`.
+2. Extend `readPreambleContext` with a required
+   `ReadonlyArray<string>` argument and include that exact list in its return
+   value. Its existing filesystem reads and tolerant stage behavior remain
+   unchanged.
+3. Pass `chat.installedHelpers` when `sendOrientationOpening` reads the
+   preamble context.
+4. Pass the same value in `sendMessage`'s first-prompt branch. This covers
+   fresh sessions and resume fallbacks.
+5. Leave the genuine-resume branch on `buildChatReorientation`; do not add a
+   helper sentence there.
+
+### 3. Render only installed slugs
+
+Replace only the existing unconditional guidance element in
+`buildChatPreamble`:
+
+- For a non-empty list, render the exact new form from the Outcome section.
+- For an empty list, contribute no array element at all.
+- Preserve the returned order and render no slug outside the list.
+- Do not change the mission, bundle-layout, pipeline, CLI, direct-project, or
+  current-step lines.
+- Do not change `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL`, `PREAMBLE_SEPARATOR`,
+  `ORIENTATION_INSTRUCTION`, or joining/newline behavior.
+
+## Tests
+
+### Focused preamble unit tests
+
+Extend, rather than replace,
+`packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts`:
+
+1. Add `installedHelpers` to the shared `PreambleContext` fixture and all
+   context literals. Pass an explicit list to `readPreambleContext` and update
+   its exact return-value assertions, preserving all existing one-liner and
+   stage tests.
+2. Replace the broad unconditional William-pointer assumption with three
+   explicit builder cases:
+   - helpers present: the bullet names both supplied slugs exactly;
+   - helpers absent: there is no guidance-skills assertion, agent-home
+     pointer, or William slug;
+   - partial install: the bullet names the supplied helper and does not name
+     the omitted helper.
+3. Keep the existing assertions for mission, configured bundle layout,
+   pipeline, CLI guidance, direct-project warning, derived current step,
+   declared-stage honesty, sentinel, separator, and orientation behavior.
+4. Add an exact non-helper-lines regression assertion. Compare the preamble
+   after removing the conditional helper bullet with the current sequence of
+   all other lines, including blank lines. Run it for the present, absent, and
+   partial contexts so omission cannot shift or rewrite unrelated content.
+5. Keep a direct assertion that the preamble itself never contains
+   `PREAMBLE_SEPARATOR`.
+
+### Existing chat-session integration test
+
+Tighten `test/e2e/chat-sessions.e2e.test.ts` without adding fixtures:
+
+1. Use its existing workspace containing only
+   `william-draft-skill-md` as the partial-install case.
+2. In the first-human-message flow, assert that the echoed full preamble names
+   `william-draft-skill-md` and does not name
+   `william-research-a-skill`.
+3. In the agent-speaks-first flow, assert the same against the opening
+   context. This catches a failure to retain the list on `LiveChat` for the
+   second full-preamble path.
+4. In the existing agent-home injection assertion, retain the positive draft
+   helper check and add a negative research-helper check, tying the preamble
+   assertions to what actually landed.
+
+The unit matrix covers present, absent, and partial inputs. The existing E2E
+partial fixture covers the production handoff and both delayed preamble
+emitters.
+
+## Validation
+
+Run focused checks first:
+
+```sh
+bun test packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts
+bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/cli
+bun test test/e2e/chat-sessions.e2e.test.ts --timeout 30000
+```
+
+Then run the repository gates:
+
+```sh
+bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/core
+bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/cli
+bun test packages
+bun run build:viewer
+bun test test/e2e --timeout 30000
+```
+
+The viewer build remains a regression gate, not a source-change requirement.
+If the focused chat E2E needs `packages/viewer/dist`, run
+`bun run build:viewer` before that test and do not retain unrelated generated
+output.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- A non-empty installation result produces exactly one guidance bullet naming
+  every returned slug and no others.
+- An empty installation result produces no guidance-skills assertion,
+  missing-helper warning, agent-home pointer, or William-family guess.
+- A partial installation names only the helper that landed.
+- Both a first human message and the agent-speaks-first opening use the real
+  session-start result.
+- A genuine resume's re-orientation remains byte-identical and gains no helper
+  mention; a resume fallback uses the fresh conditional preamble.
+- Every non-helper preamble line and blank-line boundary is byte-identical to
+  the current output.
+- `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` and `PREAMBLE_SEPARATOR` are unchanged.
+- The focused preamble tests, CLI typecheck, package tests, viewer build, and
+  E2E suite pass.
+- No files outside the three listed code/test files are changed during
+  implementation, except ignored/generated viewer build output required
+  locally for validation.
+
+## Risks and mitigations
+
+- **The helper result is lost before a delayed first prompt.** Keep the list
+  on `LiveChat` and exercise both delayed prompt paths in E2E.
+- **Conditional omission creates an extra blank line.** Omit the array
+  element with a conditional spread and compare all non-helper lines exactly.
+- **A broad family label reintroduces absent slugs.** Render only
+  `installedHelpers`, preserving its order; assert the omitted slug
+  negatively in unit and E2E coverage.
+- **A later #190 change enriches the preparation result type.** Re-read the
+  current return type before implementation. If #190 lands first, retain its
+  richer entries but render only their slug field; do not duplicate or undo
+  its source-resolution work.
+- **External mutation after session preparation makes the snapshot stale.**
+  The contract is the completed `prepareAgentHome` result for this session.
+  Filesystem watching or per-prompt rescanning would expand scope and is not
+  part of issue #196.
+
+## Explicitly out of scope and deferred
+
+- Do not fix helper source resolution or packaged-skills fallback; that is
+  issue #190.
+- Do not change `prepareAgentHome` copy, cleanup, auth-seeding, or
+  stale-destination behavior.
+- Do not add UI banners, warnings, journal events, telemetry, server response
+  fields, or persisted-session schema.
+- Do not modify viewer parsing or rendering.
+- Do not mention helpers in `buildChatReorientation`.
+- Do not edit `docs/library`.
+- Defer any broader helper-discovery model, runtime filesystem monitoring, or
+  warning surface to a separately authorized issue.

GitHub Issue #196: Chat preamble claims guidance skills are installed when seeding installed nothing

Issue URL: https://github.com/sociotechnica-org/skillmaker-studio/issues/196

## Summary

The chat preamble tells every agent "Your guidance skills are installed in your
agent home -- read the relevant william-* skill before acting." When seeding
installed nothing, that sentence is false, and the agent does what a competent
agent should: it goes looking for the skills it was promised. `prepareAgentHome`
already returns exactly the fact needed to tell the truth — `installedHelpers` —
and the call site throws it away.

## Motivation / Problem

An instruction that names an artifact which isn't there is worse than no
instruction: it converts a missing dependency into a filesystem search. In the
live session that produced this ticket, the agent's first move was
`ls ~/.skillmaker/agent-home/claude-code/skills/`, and when that came back
empty it escalated to `find / -maxdepth 8 -type d -iname "william-*"` and a
sweep of the operator's other repos. Each of those is a path outside the
project, so each one raised a permission card.

This is a *distinct* defect from the seeding bug (#190). Fixing #190 makes the
helpers present in shipped builds — but a source checkout with no packaged
skills directory, or a future helper slug that fails to resolve, will still be
announced as installed. The preamble should assert only what is true at the
moment it is written.

## Observed behavior

Fresh project on v0.6.2, chat session started on a new bundle. The agent home
contains no `skills/` directory. The preamble nonetheless states the skills are
installed, and the session opens with a multi-command hunt across the machine
for `william-*` before any bundle work begins.

## Current shape

The claim, `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts:324`:

```ts
    `- Your guidance skills are installed in your agent home -- read the relevant william-* skill before acting.`,
```

It is unconditional — a constant line in the preamble array, with no input from
whether seeding succeeded.

Meanwhile `prepareAgentHome` computes and returns precisely that
(`ChatSessions.ts:160`, `:179-181`):

```ts
): { readonly home: string; readonly installedHelpers: ReadonlyArray<string> } => {
```
```ts
    installed.push(slug);
  }
  return { home, installedHelpers: installed };
```

and both call sites discard it — `ChatSessions.ts:598` and `:793`:

```ts
    const { home } = prepareAgentHome(provider, this.root, this.config.skillsDir);
```

The trap worth naming: the information needed to be honest is already computed,
already returned, and already at the call site. This is not a missing capability;
it is a discarded return value.

## Proposed contract

The helper line is conditional on what actually installed:

| `installedHelpers` | Preamble line |
|---|---|
| non-empty | `- Your guidance skills (<slugs>) are installed in your agent home -- read the relevant one before acting.` |
| empty | line omitted entirely |

**Decisions:**

- When helpers installed, the line **names the slugs actually present**, so the
  agent reads what exists rather than guessing at a family name.
- When none installed, the line is **omitted**, not replaced with an apology.
  An agent told nothing about guidance skills proceeds on the bundle; an agent
  told they are "missing" may go hunting anyway.
- Partial installs name only the slugs that landed.
- `installedHelpers` is threaded to the preamble builder. `PreambleContext`
  gains a field; no other preamble line changes.
- The re-orientation preamble (`buildChatReorientation`, `ChatSessions.ts:349`)
  does not mention helpers today and does not gain a mention.
- No UI, no journal event, no warning surface. The scope is the preamble string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With helpers installed, the preamble states they are installed and names
      the installed slugs.
- [ ] With no helpers installed, the preamble contains no sentence asserting
      guidance skills are available anywhere.
- [ ] Partial install: only the slugs that actually landed are named.
- [ ] Negative: the preamble never names a slug absent from the agent home.
- [ ] Regression: every other preamble line — bundle layout, pipeline, CLI
      guidance, direct-in-project warning, and the derived-stage "current step"
      sentence — is byte-identical to today.
- [ ] Regression: `packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts` passes, extended
      rather than rewritten.
- [ ] Regression: `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` is unchanged — the viewer splits replayed
      first prompts on it (`chatModel.ts`).
- [ ] Tests cover: helpers-present, helpers-absent, and partial-install.

## Implementation notes

Both call sites already destructure the result; the change is to keep the second
field and pass it through. Prefer threading it into `PreambleContext` over
recomputing installation state inside the preamble builder — the builder is
deliberately synchronous and filesystem-light.

Scope fences:

- **Do not fix the seeding here.** That is #190. This issue is about the
  preamble telling the truth about whatever seeding did.
- **Do not add a user-facing warning.** A missing helper is not a condition the
  director needs a banner for.
- **Do not change `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` or the separator** — the viewer parses on
  both.

- `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts` — the claim (:324), the preamble

GitHub Issue #196: Chat preamble claims guidance skills are installed when seeding installed nothing

Issue URL: https://github.com/sociotechnica-org/skillmaker-studio/issues/196

## Summary

The chat preamble tells every agent "Your guidance skills are installed in your
agent home -- read the relevant william-* skill before acting." When seeding
installed nothing, that sentence is false, and the agent does what a competent
agent should: it goes looking for the skills it was promised. `prepareAgentHome`
already returns exactly the fact needed to tell the truth — `installedHelpers` —
and the call site throws it away.

## Motivation / Problem

An instruction that names an artifact which isn't there is worse than no
instruction: it converts a missing dependency into a filesystem search. In the
live session that produced this ticket, the agent's first move was
`ls ~/.skillmaker/agent-home/claude-code/skills/`, and when that came back
empty it escalated to `find / -maxdepth 8 -type d -iname "william-*"` and a
sweep of the operator's other repos. Each of those is a path outside the
project, so each one raised a permission card.

This is a *distinct* defect from the seeding bug (#190). Fixing #190 makes the
helpers present in shipped builds — but a source checkout with no packaged
skills directory, or a future helper slug that fails to resolve, will still be
announced as installed. The preamble should assert only what is true at the
moment it is written.

## Observed behavior

Fresh project on v0.6.2, chat session started on a new bundle. The agent home
contains no `skills/` directory. The preamble nonetheless states the skills are
installed, and the session opens with a multi-command hunt across the machine
for `william-*` before any bundle work begins.

## Current shape

The claim, `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts:324`:

```ts
    `- Your guidance skills are installed in your agent home -- read the relevant william-* skill before acting.`,
```

It is unconditional — a constant line in the preamble array, with no input from
whether seeding succeeded.

Meanwhile `prepareAgentHome` computes and returns precisely that
(`ChatSessions.ts:160`, `:179-181`):

```ts
): { readonly home: string; readonly installedHelpers: ReadonlyArray<string> } => {
```
```ts
    installed.push(slug);
  }
  return { home, installedHelpers: installed };
```

and both call sites discard it — `ChatSessions.ts:598` and `:793`:

```ts
    const { home } = prepareAgentHome(provider, this.root, this.config.skillsDir);
```

The trap worth naming: the information needed to be honest is already computed,
already returned, and already at the call site. This is not a missing capability;
it is a discarded return value.

## Proposed contract

The helper line is conditional on what actually installed:

| `installedHelpers` | Preamble line |
|---|---|
| non-empty | `- Your guidance skills (<slugs>) are installed in your agent home -- read the relevant one before acting.` |
| empty | line omitted entirely |

**Decisions:**

- When helpers installed, the line **names the slugs actually present**, so the
  agent reads what exists rather than guessing at a family name.
- When none installed, the line is **omitted**, not replaced with an apology.
  An agent told nothing about guidance skills proceeds on the bundle; an agent
  told they are "missing" may go hunting anyway.
- Partial installs name only the slugs that landed.
- `installedHelpers` is threaded to the preamble builder. `PreambleContext`
  gains a field; no other preamble line changes.
- The re-orientation preamble (`buildChatReorientation`, `ChatSessions.ts:349`)
  does not mention helpers today and does not gain a mention.
- No UI, no journal event, no warning surface. The scope is the preamble string.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With helpers installed, the preamble states they are installed and names
      the installed slugs.
- [ ] With no helpers installed, the preamble contains no sentence asserting
      guidance skills are available anywhere.
- [ ] Partial install: only the slugs that actually landed are named.
- [ ] Negative: the preamble never names a slug absent from the agent home.
- [ ] Regression: every other preamble line — bundle layout, pipeline, CLI
      guidance, direct-in-project warning, and the derived-stage "current step"
      sentence — is byte-identical to today.
- [ ] Regression: `packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts` passes, extended
      rather than rewritten.
- [ ] Regression: `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` is unchanged — the viewer splits replayed
      first prompts on it (`chatModel.ts`).
- [ ] Tests cover: helpers-present, helpers-absent, and partial-install.

## Implementation notes

Both call sites already destructure the result; the change is to keep the second
field and pass it through. Prefer threading it into `PreambleContext` over
recomputing installation state inside the preamble builder — the builder is
deliberately synchronous and filesystem-light.

Scope fences:

- **Do not fix the seeding here.** That is #190. This issue is about the
  preamble telling the truth about whatever seeding did.
- **Do not add a user-facing warning.** A missing helper is not a condition the
  director needs a banner for.
- **Do not change `PREAMBLE_SENTINEL` or the separator** — the viewer parses on
  both.

Relevant current files, as orientation only:

- `packages/cli/src/server/ChatSessions.ts` — the claim (:324), the preamble
  builder (:320-329), `prepareAgentHome` (:156-182), call sites (:598, :793)
- `packages/cli/test/ChatPreamble.test.ts` — existing coverage

---

**Related:** #190 (packaged-skills fallback for the agent home). #190 makes the
helpers present; this makes the preamble honest when they aren't.


Implement exactly this issue. Verify every claim in the issue against the current code before acting on it; the issue is a report, not a spec — the code is the truth. Stay minimal: fix the reported defect with tests, nothing adjacent.

agent_tools.name: apply_patch
agent_tools.description: Use the `apply_patch` tool to edit files. This is a FREEFORM tool, so do not wrap the patch in JSON.

agent_tools.name: close_agent
agent_tools.description: Close a running or completed subagent that is no longer needed.

agent_tools.name: request_user_input
agent_tools.description: Ask the human one or more questions and wait for their answers before continuing this stage.

agent_tools.name: send_input
agent_tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running agent receives it at a safe turn boundary. A completed agent starts another turn in the same session with its existing history.

agent_tools.name: shell_command
agent_tools.description:
Runs a shell command and returns its output.
- Always set the `workdir` param rather than using `cd`.
- Reading and searching files goes through this tool: prefer `rg` and `rg --files`, which are much faster than alternatives like `grep` and `find`.
- Use `apply_patch` to edit files, not `cat`, heredocs, or other shell write tricks.
- `timeout_ms` defaults to 10000 ms and is capped at 600000 ms. A command that timed out once will time out again, so raise the timeout rather than retrying.

agent_tools.name: spawn_agent
agent_tools.description: Spawn a subagent for independent work or context isolation. Use it for tasks that can proceed separately, and avoid duplicating the same work in the parent session.

agent_tools.name: update_plan
agent_tools.description: Update the multi-step plan for the current task. Submit the entire plan; existing steps are reconciled by exact step text.

agent_tools.name: wait
agent_tools.description: Wait for a subagent to complete, then use the result to synthesize the outcome for the user.

agent_tools.name: web_search
agent_tools.description: Search the web using Brave Search when current external information is needed. Returns result titles, URLs, and descriptions; use web_fetch for a specific URL.
